title: Feature draft — draft, review, and lock a feature's PRD and tech spec together — plan 002
epic_title: Feature draft — draft, review, and lock a feature's PRD and tech spec together

tasks.title: Authorize native requirement links in the memory reconciler
tasks.goal: A decision written natively in memory may serve a requirement claim that was itself written natively, while every claim captured from a PRD ledger keeps document-declared coverage.
tasks.current: The reconciler authorizes a serves edge only through PRD ledgers and the design index, so a native decision serving a native claim is reported as unauthorized coverage.
tasks.desired: A claim whose subject maps to no PRD ledger, at the trusted base or the candidate, is native; a native decision's serves edge to an active native claim is authorized. A serves edge from a native decision to a ledger-mapped claim stays refused. The evaluator version increments, trusted baselines replay under their own evaluator, and the rule applies only once it is at the trusted base.
scope: the native-claim predicate over PRD ledger mapping
the authorization branch for native serves edges
the evaluator version increment and historical replay
out_of_scope: every other reconciliation finding, whose classification stays byte-identical
acceptance: a native decision serving a native claim passes the memory gate with no finding
a native decision serving a ledger-mapped claim is refused as unauthorized coverage
a proposal that adds the rule and relies on it in the same change is refused by the trusted-base evaluator
the live corpus reproduces its debt ratchet exactly under the new evaluator
key_interfaces: the native-claim predicate
the serves authorization used by the reconciler's coverage check

tasks.title: Compile a draft's PRD and its documents into records
tasks.goal: A draft's PRD working file and its other documents compile in process into native memory records, deterministically.
tasks.current: Only the reconciler turns a folded PRD ledger into claims, and it tags them as document captures.
tasks.desired: The compiler reads the PRD working file in the PRD template's grammar and maps each requirement row to the claim kind the reconciler's mapping assigns, each Q row to a Question whose Resolution cell becomes its Answer, and each working file to a native literal Document holding its exact text. It computes the draft digest over the contract files. Compiled records carry no source-capture or PRD-ledger provenance. Everything except identity and issuance time is a pure function of the working files and the mainline.
scope: the PRD working-file reader and the row-to-claim mapping reuse
Q rows with their Resolution cells
native literal Documents for every working file, and the draft digest
out_of_scope: the tech spec, problems, and reviews (T3); writing records to disk (T7)
acceptance: compiling the same working files against the same mainline twice gives identical record content
each PRD row kind in the fixture maps to the claim kind the reconciler assigns to the same row
no compiled record carries a source-capture or PRD-ledger tag or a source-file provenance
an empty Resolution cell yields an open Question and a filled one yields its Answer
key_interfaces: the in-process compile entry point shared by every reader
the draft digest

tasks.title: Compile the tech spec, requirement problems, reviews, and requirement changes
tasks.goal: The rest of a draft compiles in process: tech-spec decisions serving named requirements, requirement problems with their rulings, review reports with the digest they read, and the list of requirement changes made during the draft.
tasks.current: Design decisions reach memory only through a merged design document and the design index.
tasks.desired: Each tech-spec decision compiles to a Decision serving the requirements its Serves line names. Each requirement problem compiles to a Question, and its ruling to an Answer carrying the author, reason, and triggering problem. Each review report compiles to a Document recording the draft digest it read. From the draft branch's history, every requirement row changed after it first appeared is listed with the ruling that names it, or marked unruled.

requirement problems and rulings
review reports with their recorded digest
the requirement-change list from the draft branch's history

a ruling compiles to an Answer carrying its author, reason, and triggering problem
a requirement row edited after its first commit with no ruling appears in the change list marked unruled
a review report compiles recording the draft digest it names
key_interfaces: the change list consumed by the approval request (T7)
the Serves-line grammar of the tech-spec working file

tasks.title: Judge readiness over the draft's own content
tasks.goal: `memory ready <feature>` refuses a draft whose own content is incomplete and names every unmet condition.
tasks.current: No readiness verdict exists for a draft.
tasks.desired: The verb compiles the draft in process and refuses while any open question or requirement problem lacks an answer, any Must requirement lacks a serving tech-spec decision, any requirement lacks a fit criterion or verification method, any part is unreadable, or the last PRD and tech-spec reviews did not read the version's digest or leave a blocking finding without a disposition. It prints one closed verdict naming each condition, item, and remedy, and exits non-zero when not ready. Staleness follows the design's draft digest, which covers the PRD and the tech spec: a brainstorm record edited after the last reviews does not make them stale, a scope the operator kept for UB-2 on 2026-09-24.

a draft changed after its last reviews is refused until both reviews record the new digest
a ready fixture exits zero with an empty unmet list
key_interfaces: the readiness verdict schema
the `memory ready` verb and its exit codes

tasks.title: Judge readiness over links, currency, and structure
tasks.goal: Readiness also refuses a draft that depends on superseded content, cites what does not resolve, misses a required PRD section, or holds an inconsistent link graph, with one result wherever it runs.
tasks.current: These checks exist only in the contract gate, over document machine faces.
tasks.desired: The verdict adds four conditions: no part depends on another feature's superseded or retired records; every citation resolves against memory or the document corpus; the PRD holds every section its template requires, §0 and contract readiness included; and requirement-to-decision links have no dangling target, broken supersession, or cycle. The same draft version and mainline give a byte-identical verdict locally, in hosted checks, and at the lock. The hosted readiness check runs on every pull request: it judges a draft pull request's head and passes, naming no draft, on a pull request that holds none, so the required check never blocks other proposals.

the hosted check judges a draft pull request's head and passes, naming no draft, on a pull request that holds none
key_interfaces: the readiness verdict schema, extended with the four conditions

tasks.title: Open a draft and report each feature's contract state
tasks.goal: `pyxis draft open <feature>` starts a new feature as a draft, and `pyxis draft status` reports every feature's contract state.
tasks.current: New features start as separate PRD and design documents in separate proposals.
tasks.desired: Opening creates the draft branch under the configured prefix, scaffolds the working files under the configured drafts root from the templates, and opens a code-host draft pull request; a feature that already has a PRD ledger is refused, since existing features are not migrated, and a draft-born feature that already has a locked version is refused, naming `draft reopen`. Whoever runs it, the operator included, the draft pull request is opened under the configured agent identity, because the code host never lets a pull request's author approve it; with no agent identity configured, opening refuses, naming the setup step. Status reports each feature as drafting its first version, locked at version N, drafting version N+1 while N binds, or still in the document pipeline. Nothing reaches the mainline before a lock.

tasks.title: Prepare the lock
tasks.goal: `pyxis draft prepare-lock <feature>` turns a ready draft into the exact version the operator approves.
tasks.current: No step turns working files into landed records.
tasks.desired: The step rebases the draft onto the current mainline, re-runs readiness there, compiles once, writes the records with evidence taken at that tree, stores each file's exact text, removes the working files in the same commit, renders the approval request as the pull request's description, and requests the operator's review. The approval request, rendered as the pull request's description, shows the PRD's §0, the readiness result, every requirement change with its ruling and the ruling's declared author, or marked unruled, and every declined blocking review finding with its ruling and declared author. It stays within the code host's description limit, linking whatever does not fit, and links the complete PRD and tech spec, whose exact texts the same pull request adds as literal Documents, so the approval view, the description with those Documents, misses no part of the contract. A later round reverts the preparation commit. A failed step leaves the working files unchanged and names the step.
scope: rebase, readiness re-run, one compile, and the record write
working-file removal and the revert path
the approval request as the pull request description
out_of_scope: reading the approval and the lock record (T8, T9)
a reopened draft's differences and lock guards (T21, T22)
acceptance: the preparation commit adds only records and removes every working file, and the memory gate passes at the landing tree
reverting the preparation commit restores the working files byte for byte with the same draft digest

the approval request lists every requirement change with its ruling and the ruling's declared author, the unruled one marked, and every declined blocking finding with its ruling and declared author, and on a contract larger than the code host's description limit it stays within the limit and links the complete PRD and tech spec the pull request adds
a draft whose mainline moved since its last readiness pass cannot finish preparation without the re-run
key_interfaces: the prepare-lock verb and its exit codes
the approval request rendering

The operator owns the contract record paths and the abandonment record's path, so a lock and an abandonment each need the operator's review, while a proposal adding neither keeps its merge policy, the merge lane included. The operator applies the branch protection named in the solution shape.

tasks.title: Emit and retain draft events
tasks.goal: Every draft step emits its event, and the events are retained with the lock or the abandonment record.
tasks.current: No draft events exist.
tasks.desired: Opening, a failed step, a requirement change, a refused lock, and a reopen each append their event with its fields to the draft's event log, which compiles into memory at lock preparation or rides the abandonment record; the lock record carries the lock event. Each event is emitted at its own step: the open, reopen, and abandon verbs, lock preparation, and the change listing, which emits one requirement-change event per ruling that changes a requirement, keyed by the ruling's commit so a repeated preparation emits nothing twice; abandonment runs the listing too. The checkpoint inventory (T26) reads them. This resolves the design's open question on where a draft's events live before its lock, which the design assigns to implementation, by adopting its proposed working-file event log. A failed step changes no working file: its event is written to the draft's pending-event ref, which travels with the draft branch, and is appended to the log by the next step that succeeds, from any clone, or carried by the abandonment record.

tasks.title: Lock a reopened draft by its differences
tasks.goal: A reopened draft's lock writes exactly what differs from the binding version, and each version renders in full as of its lock.
tasks.current: Lock preparation writes every compiled unit as new; nothing compares a draft with a binding version.
tasks.desired: For a reopened draft, lock preparation compares each compiled unit with the binding version's active record at its address. A new unit is written. A changed unit supersedes the active record, where a unit counts as changed when its own content or any record it relates to changed, so a decision serving a reworded requirement is re-issued. An unchanged unit writes nothing. Each record compiled from a PRD or tech-spec row the draft no longer holds is revoked, a question's answer with it, and the literal PRD and tech-spec Documents are superseded when their text changed. Problems, brainstorm records, review reports, and events of earlier versions are never superseded or revoked. Readiness judges the binding records with the draft's differences applied.

a tech-spec decision whose text is unchanged but which serves a reworded requirement is re-issued to serve the new record, and readiness finds the requirement served

tasks.title: Carry the lock basis in a feature-neutral plan header
tasks.goal: The plan header records a draft-born plan's lock basis, and a plan that no feature supplies folds and projects without feature-only fields.
tasks.current: The plan header's row set is closed and always requires PRD and Design rows naming documents, so a plan without a feature's documents cannot fold.
tasks.desired: The header gains a Basis row naming the lock record a draft-born plan was generated from, and an Intake row that names a plan no feature supplies. The feature-only rows — Feature, PRD, Design, and Basis — are required only of a feature's plan, and a non-feature plan names itself in its Intake row instead; plan-task identities and epic markers derive from whichever row names the plan, unchanged for feature plans: a draft-born plan's PRD and Design rows name the feature's memory subjects, a document-pipeline plan keeps its document paths, and a plan from a non-feature intake omits all three, citing its intent and decision in its task traces, with coverage checked only where a governing PRD exists. The plan model and the template carry the same rows. The same projection accepts every kind, and the handoff it renders carries no feature-only field.
scope: the Basis and Intake rows, the feature-only rows' conditions, and identities derived from the naming row, in the parser, the plan model, and the template

the handoff's freedom from feature-only fields

tasks.title: Accept rulings and declines only from their authority
tasks.goal: A requirement ruling counts only from the operator or from Argus under a granting authority contract, and a declined blocking finding counts only with the operator's ruling.
tasks.current: The compiler records a ruling's declared author, and readiness counts any declined finding as dispositioned.
tasks.desired: Readiness accepts a product ruling whose declared author is the operator, or Argus where its authority contract grants that act. Any other ruling is refused: readiness names it, its requirement problem stays open, and its change is listed unruled. A blocking review finding counts as dispositioned when applied, or when declined with the operator's ruling; a decline without that ruling is refused. The check reads the declared author, which is not proof of who wrote the ruling: per the operator's 2026-09-24 ruling, the operator's approval of the exact version, whose request lists every ruling with its declared author, is what vouches for each one.
scope: the ruling-authority check against the operator and Argus's authority contract
the operator-ruling check on declined blocking findings
out_of_scope: authenticating identities, which the lock approval does (T8)
acceptance: an operator ruling, and an Argus ruling under a granting authority contract, are accepted
an Argus ruling without a grant, and any other agent's ruling, are refused naming the ruling, with its problem left open
a blocking finding declined without the operator's ruling is refused, and one declined with it passes
key_interfaces: the authority conditions in the readiness verdict

tasks.title: Record the checkpoint inventory
tasks.goal: When the first three draft-born features have locked and finished implementation, the checkpoint inventory is computed and kept in memory.
tasks.current: Nothing detects the post-launch checkpoint or records its inventory.
tasks.desired: The inventory verb reports the checkpoint as not yet due, naming what is missing, until the first three draft-born features have locked and their plans' tasks have all finished. Once due, it writes one checkpoint-inventory record to memory carrying the three features, the count of new files under the document corpus's PRD, tech-design, brainstorm, and review roots for them, and their reopens by confirmed cause, read from the retained events. Running it again writes nothing new.
scope: the checkpoint trigger over locked, fully implemented draft-born features
the inventory's fields and its record in memory
out_of_scope: the adopt, iterate, or kill verdict, which the operator records
acceptance: before the trigger holds, the verb reports not yet due naming the missing condition, and writes nothing
on a fixture with three locked, fully implemented draft-born features, it writes one record carrying the features, the new corpus file count, and the reopens by cause
a second run writes nothing new
key_interfaces: the checkpoint inventory verb and its record
